# Fate UI v0.9.3-beta2

A small prerelease that fixes the in-app provider sign-in flow introduced in beta1.

## Fixed

- Browser OAuth sign-ins (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic) no longer block on the manual code prompt. The SDK's paste fallback exists for terminals where the localhost callback cannot reach the app; Fate UI was showing it as the primary step, so after finishing in the browser you were still asked for a redirect URL, and if the callback raced the prompt the flow never completed. The dialog now keeps the browser progress on screen and closes itself when the callback lands. The paste box moved into a collapsed fallback for the rare case where the OAuth callback port is blocked; submitting the authorization code or redirect URL there still finishes the flow, and progress updates can no longer clear a prompt that is still answerable.
- The sign-in dialog no longer closes itself on a stale snapshot when the provider is already connected. That race hid the browser-or-headless chooser until `/login` was typed a second time. Auto-close now waits until the flow has actually gone active and settled back to idle, shows a starting state immediately after a click, reports failed starts inline, and cancels the login when closed mid-flight instead of orphaning it.
- The provider list gets a filter search once it holds more than six entries: matches by name or id, case-insensitive, with a clear button and an empty state. Small lists stay as they were.

## Verification

- Local validation: TypeScript typecheck, 145 Vitest files / 1366 tests, production build, and packaged Windows installer passed on Windows.
- GitHub Actions run [31914316330](https://github.com/Master0fFate/pi-fategui/actions/runs/31914316330) passed on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64. Each platform built, installed, and smoked its artifacts.

## Notes

- If the collapsed paste fallback is ever needed, something is occupying the OAuth callback port (1455), typically another Codex or CLI sign-in. Close it and sign in again; the automatic path should take over.
- Public beta installers are unsigned. Verify each download against the `SHA256SUMS` file shipped with the release.
